Gardner CNRA:
The Gardner area presently contains almost exclusively single-family detached dwelling units. This is to be expected in an area which has for many decades been an established residential neighborhood. Various commercial land uses occur along the perimeters of Gardner on Willow Street and to a lesser extent along Bird Avenue. Another area of commercial uses exists along part of Delmas Avenue, the spine of the neighborhood. Before the construction of the Route 280 Highway, Delmas Avenue extended from Willow Street northerly to Santa Clara Street. It served as a main thoroughfare through the then-larger Gardner neighborhood and was a locally important neighborhood commercial area.
Mayfair CNRA:
The Mayfair neighborhood presents an interesting example of the unplanned evolution of a rural area into a suburban residential neighborhood. More discussion on this point can be found in this Urban Design section.
The Mayfair neighborhood is surrounded by major roadways, including an interstate freeway which snips off one neighborhood street from the main area. Along the northerly border, Alum Rock Avenue, strip commercial uses are complete. Elsewhere in Mayfair, residential uses predominate. San Antonio and Mayfair Elementary Schools are located at King Road and San Antonio Street and Kammerer Street and Sunset Avenue, respectively. A junior high school, Lee Mathson School is also located on Kammerer Avenue at Sinclair Drive. The Mayfair Community Center and Mayfair Park, a recent CDBG project are on Kammerer Avenue across the street from Mathson Junior High School. The Mayfair Community Center is the site of proposed expansion as part of the new three-year CDBG program. The park, a 5.19 acre site, was developed during the last CDBG program. Distinct from the other CNRA's in the project, Mayfair has a relatively high percentage of multi-family units. The entire area south of Kammerer Avenue and east of Mayfair School is devoted to duplexes. The Dobern Avenue/Berkeley Way segment is physically severed from the remainder of Mayfair by Silver Creek and the recent termination of Kammerer Avenue south of the Creek. This small sub-neighborhood, plus Sinclair Drive, exhibits a marked degree of physical deterioration. Another physically separated part of the Mayfair CNRA is a one-block long Summer Street, a dead-end road which is immediately north of Jackson Avenue and Route 680.
The portion of Mayfair generally north of San Antonio and south of Alum Rock is older and features many small lots and irregular parcelization. On some long narrow lots more than one residential unit has been constructed.
An evident land use characteristic of Mayfair is the large amount of vacant land. Some of this land has ceased being used for intensive agricultural and has not been developed. The remainder of the vacant land results from demolitions as part of the Mayfair 1 Redevelopment Project.
